# scrap-spark

Cloudflare Worker: **cached Spark AI + shared build wall for [Scrapcraft](https://github.com/SuperInstance/Scrapcraft)**.

Implements the fleet's pincher-cache doctrine — *"model call heavy at first, then
more and more canned responses"* (pattern proven in `mist-voice`):

```
POST /spark {question, context}
  hash = SHA-256(spark_version | normalized question | context)
  KV index → R2 body  ── HIT ──► D1 hits++ → reply (+ X-Cache: HIT)
  miss ──► Workers AI (llama-3.3-70b) with Spark's game system prompt
        ──► store R2 + KV + D1 ledger → reply (+ X-Cache: MISS)
```

The same question asked by a second kid, in a second classroom, is free.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | What |
|---|---|
| `POST /spark` | Spark reply `{text, program?}` with `X-Cache: HIT\|MISS` |
| `GET /daily-challenge` | Deterministic-per-UTC-day challenge + **Most Interesting Failure of the Week** |
| `GET /gallery?kind=build\|failure&order=new\|top` | Shared build wall — failures are first-class content |
| `POST /gallery` | Publish a build or an interesting failure (base64 tile JSON, shape-checked) |
| `POST /gallery/:id/like` | Applause (one per liker-hash) |
| `GET /stats` | Ledger: cache entries/hits/bytes + gallery totals |

**Safety:** the game client re-validates every program via `compile()` — raw AI
output never executes. Server-side validation is a cheap shape check only.

## Ops

```bash
npm install
wrangler r2 bucket create scrap-spark-cache
wrangler kv namespace create INDEX          # put id in wrangler.toml
wrangler d1 create scrap-spark              # put id in wrangler.toml
npm run db:init
npm run deploy
```
